item.text: {"text":"Temporal attention offers a way to retain older interactions while learning their relevance. [TemProxRec (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.09784) combines absolute and relative temporal/positional embeddings in self-attention, plus temporal-proximity contrastive learning. [LSTASRec (2025 preprint)](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=5238143) describes normalized relative-time matrices added as attention biases. A [2026 BERT4Rec session-enhancement paper](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44163-026-01554-z) combines content relevance with continuous temporal decay and jointly learned gating. These provide useful mechanisms, but their reported results do not establish improvements under the pinned RecHarness evaluation.\n\nSuggested adaptation—not a directly validated recipe: preserve one bidirectional BERT4Rec and add per-head learned biases indexed by logarithmically bucketed historical gaps, b_h(bucket(|t_i−t_j|)), before attention softmax. The foundational [TiSASRec paper](https://jiachengli1995.github.io/files/wsdm20.pdf) supports modeling interaction intervals alongside positions; borrow that mechanism without replacing the BERT4Rec backbone. For the appended mask, use a dedicated unknown-time relation and optionally key recency measured against the latest observed timestamp, t_last−t_j; never supply the held-out target timestamp. A jointly trained content-conditioned gate could let older relevant events survive rather than enforcing universal decay. Retain masked-target training, exclude target timestamps from temporal features, read the final appended-mask position under left padding, and keep all temporal parameters inside the single category checkpoint. Compare temporal bias and gating separately using macro validation HR@10."}
